messages:
Maya (CS): Heads-up — Acme reported a user that we marked deprovisioned came back as an admin this morning. They show SCIM 200s on our side, but the SSO provider did a JIT provision on login. Can engs look? :eyes:
acme-ops (customer): Right — we deactivated user `j.taylor@acme.com` at 05:12 UTC via SCIM (active:false). At 05:31 UTC they signed in via AzureAD SSO and got admin role again. Our audit shows: SCIM PATCH returned 200, then SAML SSO flow mapped `EnterpriseAdmins` group which grants Admin.
igor (eng): Can you paste the SCIM payloads and the SAML assertion attributes? specifically externalId / eduPersonPrincipalName fields.
acme-ops (customer): Paste below (sanitized):
```
SCIM PATCH /scim/v2/Users/6a4f2b
Response: 200 OK
Payload (deprovision):
{
  "schemas": [],
  "id": "6a4f2b",
  "userName": "j.taylor@acme.com",
  "active": false,
  "meta": { "lastModified": "2026-03-17T05:12:08Z" }
}
```
```
SAML Assertion (post-login): attributes received:
- nameid: j.taylor@acme.com
- external_id: 67890 (IdP)
- groups: ["Employees","EnterpriseAdmins"]
- eduPersonPrincipalName: j.taylor@acme.com
```
Maya (CS): They saw our audit show a SCIM CREATE for a new user 05:31 shortly after the SSO login, not an UPDATE. So the IdP JIT path re-provisioned instead of matching the existing deprovisioned user.
lex (platform): That suggests our SCIM matching logic missed the deactivated record when deciding to create vs update. We match on `externalId` first, then `userName`/emails. Is there a window where deactivated users are tombstoned and not visible to JIT?
sam (eng): Quick hypothesis: we soft-delete (set active:false) but still keep the resource. However our SCIM search index filters out inactive users for create-match queries. JIT provisioning probably calls our /Users endpoint with a POST when it can't find an active match. If the incoming SAML has a different external_id (IdP rotated IDs), the match on externalId fails; match on userName might be disabled for JIT to avoid merging identities.
igor (eng): Can we repro locally with AzureAD SAML assertion? If JIT is doing POST and we accept it, our downstream mapper then assigns groups -> roles (EnterpriseAdmins -> Admin role). That explains role regranting.
acme-ops (customer): In our IdP logs, external_id changed after a directory migration earlier today. We didn't expect it to matter because email stayed constant.
Maya (CS): Impact: customer had to re-remove Admin access mid-day. They want a root cause and short-term mitigation.
lex (platform): Short-term mitigation options:
- Prevent JIT creates for users who were deactivated within last N hours (block POST if a deactivated user exists with same email).
- Or prefer userName/email match in JIT if external_id mismatch but email exact match and deactivated=true.
igor (eng): We'll want to confirm behavior: does our SCIM service intentionally ignore inactive users when scanning for existing accounts? If so, changing that could reintroduce merge risk for cases where truly different accounts share email — but in most SSO flows email is authoritative.
sam (eng): Repro steps I'm going to run:
1) Create user via SCIM (active: true) -> verify id X and externalId A.
2) PATCH user active:false.
3) Simulate SAML JIT POST with same email but externalId B -> observe server response (POST vs PATCH).
4) If POST, check if we create new user and then run group->role mapping code path.
```
Simulated POST body (JIT):
POST /scim/v2/Users
{
  "userName": "j.taylor@acme.com",
  "name": {"givenName":"J","familyName":"Taylor"},
  "externalId": "B",
  "active": true,
  "groups": ["EnterpriseAdmins"]
}
```
igor (eng): Good. Also capture our auth logs where SCIM handler decides POST vs PATCH. Add debug flag `SCIM_MATCH_DETAIL=1` to trace.
acme-ops (customer): Thanks — we'll stash a copy of the SAML assertion in case you need the full signed blob.
Maya (CS): Proposed immediate customer-facing mitigation: ask Acme to turn off JIT provisioning on the IdP until we patch, or configure the IdP to preserve external_id. They prefer a server-side fix.
lex (platform): Longer-term we should: (a) prefer email-based match for JIT when an inactive record exists, (b) add a safety check that newly created users that match an inactive existing user must not get elevated roles until manual review or until a reactivation flow runs.
scim-sync-bot: New alert: potential for role regrant regression across tenants where IdP rotates external_id. I filed issue RNF-1147.
sam (eng): I'll run the repro now and post logs. If we confirm, short patch will change JIT matching order for POST flows and add a 24h quarantine where created-from-JIT cannot be auto-mapped to admin role.
igor (eng): Assign to sam, priority P1 for customer impact. Sam, can you estimate EOD fix + hotfix rollback path?
sam (eng): EOD tentative for hotfix to prefer email-match; full QA + config toggle next week.
Maya (CS): I'll tell Acme we have a mitigation plan: request IdP changes for immediate stop, we expect a hotfix today to prefer email-match which should stop re-creation. Will ask legal for temporary rollback plan. :thumbsup:
acme-ops (customer): Appreciate the quick triage. We'll keep JIT disabled for now and share logs if needed.
Maya (CS): Action items: sam -> repro + hotfix (prefer email-match for JIT, add quarantine for admin mapping). igor -> add logging flag and rollout gate. lex -> draft config toggle and opt-out for customers who want strict external_id-only matching. acme-ops -> keep JIT off until patched.
scim-sync-bot: RNF-1147 updated: attached initial repro notes.
Maya (CS): Thanks team. Keep updates in this thread. :eyes:
